en.name: Catherine of Siena
en.summary: A Dominican tertiary and mystic whose letters helped persuade the pope to return the papacy from Avignon to Rome.
en.body: Catherine, the twenty-third of twenty-five children of a Siena wool dyer, joined the Dominican tertiaries as a young woman while continuing to live at home. Despite little formal education, she became an influential spiritual writer and correspondent, dictating hundreds of letters and her mystical work The Dialogue. She travelled to Avignon to urge Pope Gregory XI to end the papacy's decades-long residence there and return to Rome, a plea historians credit with helping bring the move about in 1377. She was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1970 and later named co-patroness of Europe.
